title: Header usage cockpit
summary: Responsive usage-first Studio header, shared visual rhythm and seven bounded implementation slices. Five operator decisions settled; reconstructed before/after evidence and human sight review pending.

implementationTasks.title: Workspace usage projection
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
Read docs/header-usage-cockpit/index.html and workbench.json, AGENTS.md, frontend/AGENTS.md when applicable, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/quality/design-principles.md and docs/operations/admin-design-guideline/index.html. This is one bounded implementation slice of AGT-2913, not a request to implement the entire Dossier. Preserve the five settled operator decisions: desktop second row inside the existing header; only per-CLI weekly/current-session used percentages and today USD ledger cost in that strip; per-model breakdown in CLI detail; phone one row with primary weekly percentage and today cost; workspace-local calendar with UTC detail. Do not add a global model chip, standalone banner or horizontal header scrolling. Preserve model-routing correctness floors. Use central tokens/shared components, text-only menus, no decorative left accent bars and both themes. Git ownership remains with the platform.

Slice: HUC-S1 / Workspace usage projection

Deliver the read-only data projection and accounting contract in the Dossier Data contract section. Reuse quota, normalized token ledger, active run and slot sources. Propose GET /api/usage/cockpit or extend the existing equivalent owner with normal workspace authorization. Include source freshness/coverage, local day and week UTC boundaries, reset instants, per-project exact totals including unattributed values, route provenance, deduplicated live costs and optional existing budgets. AGT-2882 normalization is a prerequisite: consume normalized uncached input/cacheRead; do not double-subtract cached input or count receipts twice. UI integration is outside this slice.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract fixtures cover Codex raw input 1000 with 400 cached becoming 600 uncached plus 400 cache-read priced once; already normalized input remains unchanged.
- Today/week totals equal project children including unattributed and active receipts; duplicate bus/receipt data is counted once, and partial coverage is distinct from zero.
- Workspace-local day and configurable week boundaries handle midnight, DST and workspace changes; provider reset periods stay intact.
- Endpoint handles independent source failure and exposes effective route versus configured route. Add focused backend contract tests and document the endpoint.

Finish with changed files, checks and evidence paths. Scope outside these criteria stays in sibling cards.

Slice: HUC-S2 / Shared usage chips

After HUC-S1, implement the CLI, cost and expanded-only slot chip components using the central token scale and existing button/popover primitives. Each CLI chip owns its weekly and current-session window as an indivisible unit. Cost uses a USD ledger estimate, not quota conversion. Include normal/loading/unknown/stale/suspicious states and long-number formatting. The slot chip belongs only in expanded usage. Do not integrate responsive shell layout in this slice.

Acceptance criteria:
- Normal chips share baseline, radius and height in light/dark; no gradients, nested mini pills, decorative provider tiles or left accent bars.
- Every chip is one focusable native button with a complete accessible name; unsupported windows and missing cost never appear as zero.
- Values above 100%, long provider names, large USD totals and fractional percentages preserve full numeric units and exact detail values.
- Focused Playwright component/fixture coverage and screenshots verify both themes, focus and state labels.

Finish with changed files, checks and evidence paths. Scope outside these criteria stays in sibling cards.

Slice: HUC-S3 / Usage detail and ledger navigation

After HUC-S1 and HUC-S2, deliver CLI and cost detail opened from the chips. Use a desktop anchored nonmodal dialog popover and phone modal sheet with the same content. Show both quota windows/reset times, local and UTC timestamps, today/week project splits, coverage, live runs and included-in-totals labels, expanded-only slots, and grouped observed models/reasoning with configured-route differences. Link into the existing usage/settings hub and token ledger with scope filters. Reuse existing destinations rather than recreating the retired CLI usage surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- One chip action reaches every required detail; all project rows including unattributed reconcile with totals and active costs are identified as already included.
- Ledger navigation preserves workspace and date range. Provider reset instants are shown in workspace local time and UTC.
- Effective model and reasoning are per run and grouped within CLI; unknown data is explicit and never inherited from a global default.
- Playwright proves Enter/Space, Escape, focus return including breakpoint changes, desktop focus exit, phone focus trap/background inertness, and screenshots in both themes.

Finish with changed files, checks and evidence paths. Scope outside these criteria stays in sibling cards.

Slice: HUC-S4 / Responsive header integration

After HUC-S2 and HUC-S3, integrate the cockpit inside the existing Studio header. Implement the Dossier responsive table and content-fit fallback. Desktop is 44px navigation plus 40px usage; touch tablet uses 48px rows; phone is one 48px row with 44px targets. Place all optional navigation in a text-only overflow menu and move secondary CLIs as complete units to Details. Primary order follows selected CLI, saved default then stable provider order. Keep counters and models outside the strip.

Acceptance criteria:
- At 390, 1024 and 1728 CSS px, both themes show the settled composition; phone shows only primary weekly quota and today cost as numeric usage metrics.
- At 320 CSS px, 200% zoom, long labels and large amounts no header value clips, wraps mid-value or causes horizontal scrolling.
- Overflow retains all destinations; hidden chips leave focus order; container constraints apply the same priority rules as viewport breakpoints.
- Playwright verifies header row heights/minima, coarse-pointer targets, whole-value fit, keyboard navigation and focus restoration with screenshots.

Finish with changed files, checks and evidence paths. Scope outside these criteria stays in sibling cards.

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:

Slice: HUC-S5 / Usage alarm transitions

After HUC-S1 through HUC-S4, implement the Dossier chip-state matrix. Fresh quota used strictly above 80% warns; explicit provider-limited state takes precedence; configured daily/weekly USD budget exceeded warns on cost. Use existing budget settings; do not invent financial limits or new routing behavior. Unknown/partial data must not claim safety. Surface hidden-provider alarms through a nonnumeric state marker and accessible explanation without adding another primary number.

Acceptance criteria:
- Boundary tests cover 80 versus 80.1, values above 100, absent budget, exact budget equality, daily and weekly overruns, stale and suspicious readings and provider limits at low percentages.
- Each transition is announced politely once per source/window/reset cycle, not each refresh. Trusted recovery clears state; stale data cannot clear a limit.
- Both themes combine semantic tint with text/shape; ordinary headroom is neutral and resolved history stays quiet.
- Playwright screenshots cover quota warning, cost warning, limited, stale, partial and unknown states, including a hidden-provider alarm on phone. Routing and model pins remain unchanged.

Finish with changed files, checks and evidence paths. Scope outside these criteria stays in sibling cards.

Slice: HUC-S6 / Board and task protocol rhythm

After HUC-S4, apply the bounded maturity pass shown in the Dossier to board and task detail only. Align board tasks to lane headings, reduce repeated frames, share count styling and spacing; preserve the canonical lane presentation source and visible-child count invariant. Use flat task protocol sections and aligned timestamps, with contextual facts as a secondary column on wide layouts and a stacked region on phone. Preserve current actions, content and run-switcher history. No new tabs, metrics grids or broad admin restyling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Board lane totals equal visible task children and use canonical lane names/tones; phone lane selection navigates without moving tasks.
- Task protocol retains chronology, existing actions and archived run selection; facts stack without obscuring task controls.
- All touched surfaces use central spacing, typography and theme tokens; no status accent bars or unnecessary card nesting.
- Relevant board/detail Playwright behavior tests pass and light/dark captures at 390, 1024 and 1728 show the scoped changes.

Finish with changed files, checks and evidence paths. Scope outside these criteria stays in sibling cards.

Slice: HUC-S7 / Cockpit visual and accessibility matrix

After HUC-S1 through HUC-S6, add the integration evidence gate for the delivered cockpit, board and task detail. Use deterministic pinned demo data through the existing Playwright fixture; in task worktrees dev backend startup is allowed only from the approved Playwright dev-backend fixture. Capture product UI, not the offline concept mockup. Persist screenshots under the implementation task results folder and label provenance correctly. Reuse relevant coverage from earlier slices rather than duplicating it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Header, board and task detail have 18 after-state captures: 3 surfaces × 3 widths (390/1024/1728) × 2 themes, plus expanded/state evidence.
- Geometry assertions reject mid-value clipping, horizontal header overflow, lost primary figures, inconsistent row heights or inaccessible overflow at boundary widths and 200% zoom.
- Keyboard, accessible names, focus return/trapping, reduced motion and coarse-pointer target tests pass; record measured contrast for text and focus in both themes.
- Page errors fail capture. Data fixtures verify local/UTC resets, DST, cost reconciliation, active-spend inclusion and partial coverage; report limitations without claiming human sight review.
